mu-5cce7a23.stem: Between which muscle layers do the intercostal vein, artery and nerve run?
options: Between the skin and the external intercostal
Between the external and internal intercostals
Between serratus anterior and the external intercostal
Between the internal intercostal and the innermost intercostal
Between the innermost intercostal and the parietal pleura
mu-5cce7a23.explanation: The neurovascular bundle lies in the costal groove on the lower border of the rib, between the internal and innermost intercostals; from above down the order is vein, artery, nerve (VAN).

mu-6f0e2899.stem: Which structures pass through the aortic hiatus?
options: Aorta, thoracic duct and azygos vein
Inferior vena cava and right phrenic nerve
Oesophagus and the anterior and posterior vagal trunks
Aorta, vagus nerve and sympathetic trunk
mu-6f0e2899.explanation: The three large openings of the diaphragm: caval opening (T8) – IVC and branches of the right phrenic nerve; oesophageal hiatus (T10) – oesophagus and vagal trunks; aortic hiatus (T12) – aorta, thoracic duct and usually the azygos vein. The aortic hiatus actually lies behind the diaphragm, between the crura.

mu-4e300703.stem: After a traffic accident, a patient with a ruptured spleen complains of pain at the tip of the left shoulder (Kehr's sign). Which nerve carries this referred pain?
mu-4e300703.explanation: Sensation from the central diaphragm and the peritoneum beneath it is carried by the phrenic nerve to segments C3–C5. The skin of the shoulder is also from the C4 dermatome; when blood under the diaphragm irritates the peritoneum, pain is referred to the shoulder tip.

mu-506f3b78.stem: Which of the following about the diaphragm is FALSE?
options: When it contracts its domes descend and the thoracic cavity enlarges.
An important part of its motor supply comes from the lower intercostal nerves.
The medial arcuate ligament passes over psoas major.
The right dome is higher than the left because of the liver.
The right crus encircles the oesophageal hiatus.
mu-506f3b78.explanation: The diaphragm's only motor nerve is the phrenic nerve (C3–C5). The lower intercostal nerves carry only sensation from its periphery. The right crus is larger, and most of the fibres encircling the oesophageal hiatus come from it.

mu-82a50928.stem: Below the arcuate line, which statement about the rectus sheath is true?
options: The sheath has no anterior wall.
The internal oblique aponeurosis splits to enclose the muscle.
Its posterior wall is formed by quadratus lumborum.
The aponeuroses of the three flat muscles pass in front of the muscle; the posterior wall is formed only by the transversalis fascia.
The transversus abdominis aponeurosis passes behind the muscle.
mu-82a50928.explanation: At about the midpoint between the umbilicus and symphysis (arcuate line) the posterior sheath ends. Below this level all the aponeuroses pass in front; rectus is covered behind only by the transversalis fascia and peritoneum. The inferior epigastric artery enters the sheath just below this line.

mu-8f56cfc4.stem: At inguinal hernia surgery the sac is seen to enter the deep inguinal ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels and descend within the spermatic cord to the scrotum. Which hernia is this?
mu-8f56cfc4.explanation: An indirect hernia enters through the deep ring (lateral to the epigastric vessels), follows the canal and may descend to the scrotum; it is usually due to a patent processus vaginalis (congenital). A direct hernia emerges medial to the epigastric vessels through Hesselbach's triangle, pushing the posterior wall of the canal forwards.

mu-57b5ccfe.stem: What are the boundaries of Hesselbach's (inguinal) triangle?
options: Superior epigastric artery, linea alba and lacunar ligament
Latissimus dorsi, external oblique and iliac crest
Inguinal ligament, sartorius and adductor longus
Inferior epigastric artery, lateral border of rectus abdominis and the inguinal ligament
Spermatic cord, inguinal ligament and linea semilunaris
mu-57b5ccfe.explanation: Hesselbach's triangle is a weak area on the inner surface of the anterior abdominal wall through which direct inguinal hernias emerge. Laterally lies the inferior epigastric artery, medially the lateral border of rectus, and below the inguinal ligament.

mu-45c18444.stem: From which muscle does the cremaster arise, and which nerve supplies it?
options: Internal oblique – genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve
mu-45c18444.explanation: The cremaster fibres separate from the lower border of the internal oblique and wrap the spermatic cord. Elevation of the testis when the inner thigh is touched (cremasteric reflex) is mediated by the genitofemoral nerve (L1–L2).

mu-128c932e.stem: Which muscles form the falx inguinalis (conjoint tendon)?
mu-128c932e.explanation: The lower aponeurotic fibres of the internal oblique and transversus unite and attach to the pecten pubis, reinforcing the medial posterior wall of the inguinal canal. This is important in preventing direct hernias.

mu-d7f3b55d.stem: The inguinal ligament is the rolled-under lower border of which structure?
options: Muscle fibres of the internal oblique
mu-d7f3b55d.explanation: The aponeurosis of the external oblique folds inwards between the ASIS and the pubic tubercle to form the inguinal ligament. The triangular opening in the same aponeurosis is the superficial inguinal ring.

mu-547502a2.stem: Which muscle contributes importantly to faecal continence by maintaining the anorectal angle?
mu-547502a2.explanation: Puborectalis, part of levator ani, forms a U-shaped sling behind the rectum and pulls the anorectal junction forwards, creating an angle of about 90°. In defecation it relaxes and straightens the angle.

mu-e433086d.stem: Which is one of the main functions of quadratus lumborum?
options: To rotate the trunk to the opposite side
To fix the 12th rib during deep inspiration
mu-e433086d.explanation: Quadratus lumborum runs from the iliac crest to the 12th rib and the lumbar transverse processes. By holding the 12th rib down it helps the diaphragm contract effectively; acting on one side it bends the trunk sideways.

mu-cfcd17d2.stem: Which muscle initiates the first 15° of abduction of the arm?
mu-cfcd17d2.explanation: Supraspinatus initiates abduction while pressing the humeral head into the glenoid cavity. Between 15° and 90° deltoid dominates; above 90° the scapula must rotate upwards through trapezius and serratus anterior.

mu-3164df94.stem: Which rotator cuff muscles rotate the arm externally?
mu-3164df94.explanation: Infraspinatus (suprascapular nerve) and teres minor (axillary nerve) attach to the posterior facets of the greater tubercle and are the main external rotators of the arm. Subscapularis, teres major, latissimus and pectoralis major rotate internally.
